Tasks span 44 occupations, research and analysis deliverables being the plurality.

task_description: Compete live in AtCoder Heuristic Contest 058, a production-planning optimization problem, submitting a program within the four-hour window against the human field.
performance_evidence: ALE-Agent placed 1st on the contest's own standings, ahead of all 804 rated human entrants; 1,317 entries are listed and 804 is the rated field Sakana calls the participants. The top rated human's official performance is 3535 and the 804 average 1384, so the mean entrant reaches 39% of the standing the agent surpassed.
source_dataset: Sakana AI ALE-Agent, AtCoder Heuristic Contest 058
source_record: Sakana AI report of 2026-01-05 on the AHC058 run of 2025-12-14: 2,654 GPT-5.2 high-reasoning calls, 2,119 Gemini 3 Pro Preview high-thinking calls, about $1,000 in API fees within a $1,300 total; AtCoder contest ahc058, account fishylene, place 1; official results in research/ale-bench/build_rows.py; performance: the same standings
notes: Compute inverts the reported API spend: per-call input and output come from the ALE-Bench leaderboard's measured one-shot calls by these same two configurations, scaled by 0.771 so the call counts price to $1,000 at December 2025 list rates. The unscaled cadence gives 1.30x, which prices to the $1,300 all-in figure. Gemini 3 Pro contributes 45% of the tokens; model_id wrote the winning submission. compute_flops and ai_cost_usd are one observation, not two, since the FLOPs invert the spend. Human time is the contest window, which bounds entrants' effort but does not measure it. The agent generated candidate solutions in parallel with two frontier models, evaluated them locally and refined them without human intervention.

task: Solve one unseen ARC-AGI-3 environment on first exposure (Provider Adapter harness, high reasoning)
task_description: Play an unfamiliar puzzle-game environment from the first frame to the end, with no instructions about the goal or the rules, working out the mechanics as you go.
performance_evidence: RHAE normalises a level's action count to the median human who completed it, squared and capped at 1.15, so it censors at parity. This run scored 99.95% over the 55 semi-private environments, all solvable by humans on first exposure. Uncensored on the public set it used 41.3% of the baseline actions, beating it on 95.6% of levels.
source_dataset: ARC-AGI-3 Semi-Private leaderboard, GPT-6 Astra, September 2026
source_record: arcprize.org leaderboard v3.json entry openai-gpt-6-astra-high-provider-adapter, ARC-AGI-3 Semi-Private, 55 environments, score 0.99946, cost 18816.63, payload generated 2026-09-04. Donor mix from the 25 ARC-AGI-3 Public Demo runs of the same configuration, session GUIDs in research/arc-agi-3/astra-public-demo-runs.csv; performance: ARC-AGI-3 technical report sections 4.1 and 5, and https://arcprize.org/blog/astra
notes: No token counts are published for the semi-private runs. Compute inverts the published cost at Astra list prices under ARC's own cost model, which prices the gross input counter at the input rate and carries no cached rate in either of its benchmarking repositories. Output per gross input and the cached share are measured on the 25 public-demo runs of the same configuration, whose per-call counters are published. Cache reads priced at $1/M instead: 1.80x. The ruled 100-600B size range gives 0.33-2.0x; attention over the 127k context, omitted by the convention, adds 0.6-1.4x.

performance_evidence: RHAE normalises a level's action count to the median human who completed it, squared and capped at 1.15, so 100% is human parity. This run scored 54.82% over the 55 semi-private environments, all solvable by humans on first exposure. A random policy solves a level under once in 10,000 tries, so the chance floor is ~0.
source_dataset: ARC-AGI-3 Semi-Private leaderboard, GPT-6 Astra, September 2026
source_record: arcprize.org leaderboard v3.json entry openai-gpt-6-astra-high, ARC-AGI-3 Semi-Private, 55 environments, score 0.54819, cost 40704.72, payload generated 2026-09-04. Donor mix from the 25 ARC-AGI-3 Public Demo runs of the same configuration, session GUIDs in research/arc-agi-3/astra-public-demo-runs.csv; performance: ARC-AGI-3 technical report sections 4.1 and 5, and https://arcprize.org/blog/astra
notes: No token counts are published for the semi-private runs. Compute inverts the published cost at Astra list prices under ARC's own cost model, which prices the gross input counter at the input rate and carries no cached rate in either of its benchmarking repositories. Output per gross input and the cached share are measured on the 25 public-demo runs of the same configuration, whose per-call counters are published. Cache reads priced at $1/M instead: 1.18x. The ruled 100-600B size range gives 0.33-2.0x; attention over the 144k context, omitted by the convention, adds 0.6-1.2x. Run under ARC's Standard harness rather than the Provider Adapter.

task: RE-Bench ML research engineering environment, 2-hour budget
task_description: Take on one open-ended ML research-engineering problem — from writing a fast GPU kernel to scaffolding a model for a coding contest — and improve a weak starting solution as much as you can in 2 hours.
performance_evidence: Mean normalized score over the seven environments, best of four 30-minute runs: 0.175, against 0.077 for a human expert two hours into an 8-hour attempt. The AI is 2.3 times the human score on a metric whose floor is the starting solution. The human side is 71 attempts by 61 ML experts, read off their score logs at the 2-hour mark.

A competent adult folds a button-up shirt essentially always, so the AI does the job at a materially lower completion rate. No human result is reported.
source_record: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14759 Figures 7 and 8, Section VI-A; research/physical-intelligence/physical-intelligence.md#throughput-read-off
notes: Compute is 3600/throughput robot-seconds at 2.5 action chunks per second, times the per-chunk operation count for three 448-pixel cameras and five denoising steps. The executed-steps assumption alone moves compute by -20%/+33%. Throughput counts successes over the whole evaluation, so the figure includes time spent on failed attempts; the human estimate is for one completion. Parallel-jaw grippers and human hands differ. Run by the RL specialist on a static bimanual platform.

source_record: SWE-Marathon v1.1 leaderboard at https://swe-marathon.org, task embedding-eval, GPT-6-astra (high) under Codex; trials embedding-eval-1277;embedding-eval-1276;embedding-eval-1275;embedding-eval-1274;embedding-eval-1273;embedding-eval-1271;embedding-eval-1272;embedding-eval-1270; benchmark paper arXiv 2606.07682; performance: the same leaderboard's per-trial binary reward; research/swe-marathon/swe-marathon.md#source
notes: The published per-rollout token total is the whole prefix re-read on every call plus the output. Processed positions are rebuilt as 2C/k from the counted total and the measured API turn count, 115 turns on these trials, giving 48k positions against 2.8M counted tokens; the mean attended context is measured as C/k rather than assumed. The implied trajectory length 48k fits inside the 400k context window, so no compaction is needed for the linear-growth inversion to hold. Output tokens measured off the published trajectories are 0.64% of the counted total, against the paper's 0.53% for the whole corpus, and 37% of the rebuilt processed positions, leaving the rest as fresh tool-result input. The attached H100 runs all-MiniLM-L6-v2 over the 37 datasets each time the agent re-runs its evaluator; that GPU work is outside compute_flops. Median tokens per trial vary by up to 12x across scaffolds holding the model fixed, which is why the row is one task x one agent-model configuration and not one per model.

task: Learn to solve the Dubey platform game, original rendering
task_description: Train a game agent from scratch, by curiosity alone, to solve one level of a platform game in its original rendering, with no instruction beyond which keys steer.
performance_evidence: Both the human subjects and the agent solved the level, which is the game's only success criterion. Forty subjects finished in just under one minute, about 3000 action inputs; the agent needed about 4 million action inputs. Both sides end on the game's own terminal reward for reaching the princess; there is no score to compare.

task: Keep lane and follow traffic for one minute
task_description: Keep a car centered in its lane and following the car ahead for one minute of highway driving — steering and speed, no lane changes or turns.
performance_evidence: openpilot is a supervised Level 2 system by comma's own documentation: an adaptive cruise control and automated lane centering system whose first design requirement is that the driver can immediately retake manual control, with a driver monitoring model running alongside to enforce it. The human baseline is a licensed driver keeping lane and following traffic for the same minute with no supervisor. Below rather than match because the driving is completed only under supervision the human does not need. Consumer Reports' November 2020 evaluation of active driving assistance systems ranked the comma two running openpilot first of seven systems tested, ahead of Cadillac Super Cruise and Tesla Autopilot, on capability and performance, keeping the driver engaged, ease of use, clarity about when it is safe to use, and response to an unresponsive driver. That is a ranking against commercial Level 2 peers, not against an unsupervised driver. Fleet telemetry reported by comma in September 2026: 20,000+ users, over 300 million miles driven with a device running openpilot, over 56% of those miles driven by openpilot. comma's stated precondition for calling openpilot 1.0, at least 1,000 hours between unplanned disengagements, is not met.

notes: Single road camera. 460,656,304 multiply-accumulates per inference over 1,200 inferences per minute at the 20 Hz rate fixed by DT_MDL. The Consumer Reports evaluation tested this era's model on the comma two. Driver monitoring, camera warping and the non-neural controllers are outside the count.
